description:
Make `jit invariant check` compute enforcement drift from captured declarations through the same function the validation report uses, and fail on an unloadable gate registry as the report does.

## Background

- `check_invariants` (`crates/jit/src/commands/invariant.rs:54-64`) calls the executor's `compute_drift_findings` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:1387-1440`), which loads rules and gates from disk and treats an unparseable `gates.toml` as an unloadable source.
- The report's drift pass (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:600-629`) runs over captured declarations; an unparseable `gates.toml` fails declaration loading there, so `jit validate` fails with an error naming the file.
- `test_check_reports_unloadable_gate_registry` (`crates/jit/tests/cli_item_validate/invariant_check_cli_tests.rs:225`) pins the tolerant behaviour; the unit tests at `invariant.rs:110-157` cover drift cases.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `check_invariants` captures the repository's declarations once and computes `DriftFinding`s through the validation-layer drift function the report's drift pass calls; it no longer calls `compute_drift_findings`.
- [hard] REQ-02: An unparseable `gates.toml` makes `jit invariant check` fail with an error naming `.jit/gates.toml`; the rewritten CLI test asserts it and fails on today's code, which reports an unloadable-gate drift finding.
- [hard] REQ-03: Drift findings, the unloadable-rules case included, are otherwise unchanged, and the other invariant tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: an unloadable gate registry is an error for `jit invariant check`, as it is for `jit validate`.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Invariant check computes drift from captured declarations
